# Ezekiel 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** On August 14, in the seventh year of our exile, some of Israel's leaders came to ask the LORD for guidance. They sat down in front of me.

**2** Then the LORD spoke to me:

**3** "Son of man, tell the leaders of Israel: The Lord GOD says: Have you come to ask Me for guidance? As surely as I live, I will not let you consult Me, declares the Lord GOD.

**4** Are you willing to judge them, son of man? Then confront them with the disgusting sins of their ancestors!

**5** Tell them: The Lord GOD says: When I chose Israel, I made a solemn promise to the descendants of Jacob. I revealed Myself to them in Egypt and swore, 'I am the LORD your God.'

**6** That day I promised to bring them out of Egypt to a land I had scouted for them — a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful land in the world.

**7** I told them, 'Get rid of every disgusting idol you've become attached to! Don't defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.'

**8** But they rebelled and refused to listen. Not one of them got rid of their idols or gave up the gods of Egypt. I was ready to pour out My fury on them right there in Egypt.

**9** But I held back — for the sake of My reputation. I didn't want My name dishonored among the nations who had watched Me rescue Israel from Egypt.

**10** But they rebelled against Me again. They refused to follow My laws, rejected My commands — the very commands that give life to those who obey them — and they treated My Sabbaths with contempt.

**48** But they rebelled against Me again. They refused to follow My laws, rejected My commands — the very commands that give life to those who obey them — and they treated My Sabbaths with contempt.

**49** Then I said, 'Lord GOD, they're complaining about me! They say I just speak in riddles and parables!'

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **20:5-9**: God's history lesson is devastating — Israel didn't start rebelling in the wilderness. They were already rebels IN Egypt. There was never a golden age of obedience. God's faithfulness has always outrun Israel's.

- **20:25**: This is one of the most unsettling verses in the Bible — God gave them rules that couldn't bring life? The point seems to be that when people are determined to misread God's instructions, He lets them — and the consequences are horrifying.

- **20:32-33**: Israel wants to blend in with the nations. God says: 'Not happening. I will be your king — with fury if necessary.' God's refusal to let Israel go is both terrifying and, in a strange way, deeply loving.

— PNEUMA
